overall_formula: Arithmetic mean of the seven criterion scores, rounded to two decimal places. Do not average requirement statuses or apply an undisclosed penalty.
recommendation_rule: Any explicit critical constraint contradiction prevents a ready recommendation even when the arithmetic mean is high. Use revise for remediable omissions and do_not_accept_as_written for critical contradictions. A recommendation is separate from the overall arithmetic score.

anchors.2: Acknowledges the general domain but misses important client context.
anchors.3: Understands the main objective with limited connection to operational priorities.
anchors.4: Accurately connects the proposed approach to client context and priorities.
anchors.5: Demonstrates precise understanding of the objective, operating context and relevant trade-offs.

anchors.2: Generic feature list with unclear outputs or boundaries.
anchors.3: Main outputs are named but important boundaries or acceptance details remain vague.
anchors.4: Specific outputs and boundaries with only minor ambiguities.
anchors.5: Concrete, testable deliverables with explicit scope boundaries and acceptance approach.

criteria.name: Pricing Clarity

anchors.1: Price is absent or entirely deferred.
anchors.2: A headline estimate leaves major inclusions or recurring charges unknown.
anchors.3: A usable total is provided but the breakdown or included period has gaps.
anchors.4: An internally consistent total and breakdown identify the main inclusions and recurring costs.
anchors.5: Transparent, internally consistent cost breakdown covers the requested period, assumptions and treatment of additional scope.

criteria.note: Judge transparency here. Budget breaches belong in requirement compliance and findings; a clearly priced noncompliant offer can still score highly for pricing clarity.

criteria.name: Timeline Clarity

anchors.2: General duration or aspiration without a usable schedule.
anchors.3: Delivery date and some stages are given but sequencing or dependencies are unclear.
anchors.4: Clear relative or absolute milestones and sequencing with minor gaps.
anchors.5: Clear milestone schedule, acceptance gates and dependencies make the delivery sequence explicit.

criteria.note: Judge clarity here. Do not infer impossibility from a short timeline alone. Explicitly skipping a required pilot or acceptance gate is a compliance failure even if the schedule is clear.

anchors.1: Most important requirements are absent or contradicted, or multiple central constraints are explicitly violated.
anchors.2: Some requirements are covered but major gaps or a central constraint violation remain.
anchors.3: Most requirements are addressed with material partial coverage or unresolved omissions.
anchors.4: All key requirements are addressed, with minor omissions or ambiguity.
anchors.5: All stated requirements, including budget and timeline constraints, are explicitly and coherently addressed.

criteria.name: Tone & Persuasiveness

anchors.1: Confusing, inappropriate or almost entirely empty sales language.
anchors.2: Readable but generic, poorly tailored or dependent on unsupported superlatives.
anchors.3: Professional and partly tailored, with uneven evidence or excessive promotional language.
anchors.5: Consistently clear and persuasive through relevant specifics and balanced reasoning.

criteria.note: Length, confidence, AI terminology and polished formatting are not evidence of suitability. Do not require unprovided customer references.

anchors.1: No material risks or assumptions disclosed, or unsupported risk-free guarantees.
anchors.2: Generic caveats without concrete dependencies or mitigations.
anchors.3: Relevant risks or assumptions are named but ownership, mitigation or impact is incomplete.
anchors.4: Material dependencies and risks are specific, with sensible mitigations or schedule/cost implications.
anchors.5: Clear assumptions, limitations, owners and mitigations explain the delivery consequences of unmet dependencies.

status_precedence_note: Use contradicted if an explicit conflict exists. Otherwise missing means absent; partial means incomplete coverage; unsubstantiated means an unsupported commitment; met means a sufficiently specific and consistent response.
calibration_note: Expected score intervals are provisional synthetic annotations. They are not measured scorer outputs or statistically validated acceptance limits. Do not force an overall ordering between weak and overpromised.
